note: Which multi-character letters each language has, and whether its word list has been checked for them. The test is whether the sequence is a LETTER OF THE ALPHABET, not merely one sound spelled with two characters — otherwise German SCH and English TH would qualify and the alphabet lesson would be nonsense. Marked letters go in ALPHABETS in game_config.gd and in the word list as MOU[CH]A; see data/words/README.md. 'decided' is whether anyone has actually ruled on this language: an empty 'letters' list with decided=false means candidates exist and nobody has chosen yet, which is not the same as having none.

cs.note: CH is the 15th letter of the Czech alphabet. 8 of 277 words carry it.

sk.note: All three are letters of the 46-letter Slovak alphabet. CH in CHLIEB, UCHO, CHROBÁK; DZ in the imperatives JEDZ and POVEDZ, where it is one sound. DŽ does not occur in the current corpus.

pl.note: CZ, SZ, RZ, DZ, DŹ, DŻ and CH are dwuznaki — digraphs, and each one sound — but the Polish alphabet has 32 letters and none of them is a digraph. Not marked, on the same test that rejects Spanish CH and German SCH. This is a reversible decision: Polish reading instruction does teach dwuznaki as units, so if the game should follow the classroom rather than the alphabet, mark them and add them to ALPHABETS together. It would affect 46 of 169 words.
pl.revisit_if: a Polish teacher says the alphabet lesson should teach dwuznaki as single collectibles

de.note: SCH, CH, EI, IE, EU, PF, ST and SP are all sounds rather than letters; the German alphabet is A–Z plus Ä Ö Ü ß. CH alone appears in 42 of 178 words and would be wrong in every one.

en.note: CH, SH, TH, PH, CK and NG are sounds, not letters. SCHOOL is the reminder of why: its CH is not even the CH sound.

vi.note: Undecided, and it matters more here than anywhere else. CH, GH, GI, KH, NG, NGH, NH, PH, QU, TH, TR are taught in Vietnamese schools as units a child learns whole. Whether they belong in the alphabet for this game is a question for a Vietnamese teacher, not for a dictionary. The test is whether the sequence is a LETTER OF THE ALPHABET, not merely one sound spelled with two characters.

hu.note: These really are letters: each has its own name, its own place in the alphabet and its own section in a dictionary. DZS is three characters and one letter. The word list must be marked accordingly. The test is whether the sequence is a LETTER OF THE ALPHABET, not merely one sound spelled with two characters.

nl.note: IJ is the real question and is left out for now: it capitalises as a pair and many schools call it a letter, but it is not in the official alphabet. A native speaker should settle it — if IJ becomes a letter here it must also be marked in the word list. The test is whether the sequence is a LETTER OF THE ALPHABET, not merely one sound spelled with two characters.

es.note: CH and LL were letters of the Spanish alphabet until 2010 and are not any more. Two letters each. The test is whether the sequence is a LETTER OF THE ALPHABET, not merely one sound spelled with two characters.

pt.note: None. LH, NH and CH are one sound written with two letters, which is not the same as being a letter. The test is whether the sequence is a LETTER OF THE ALPHABET, not merely one sound spelled with two characters.

fr.note: None. CH, OU and the rest are spellings, not letters of the alphabet. The test is whether the sequence is a LETTER OF THE ALPHABET, not merely one sound spelled with two characters.

tr.note: None. Turkish spelling is one letter per sound. The test is whether the sequence is a LETTER OF THE ALPHABET, not merely one sound spelled with two characters.

it.note: None. CH, GH, GL, GN, SC are one sound written with two letters, which is not the same as being a letter. The test is whether the sequence is a LETTER OF THE ALPHABET, not merely one sound spelled with two characters.

ro.note: None. CE, CI, GE, GI, CHE, CHI, GHE, GHI are letter groups taught for reading, not letters. The test is whether the sequence is a LETTER OF THE ALPHABET, not merely one sound spelled with two characters.

uk.note: None. ДЖ and ДЗ are two letters each. The test is whether the sequence is a LETTER OF THE ALPHABET, not merely one sound spelled with two characters.

el.note: None. The δίψηφα — ΑΙ, ΕΙ, ΟΙ, ΟΥ, ΜΠ, ΝΤ, ΓΚ — are pairs making one sound, taught as such but not letters. The test is whether the sequence is a LETTER OF THE ALPHABET, not merely one sound spelled with two characters.

sv.note: None. Å, Ä and Ö are single letters, not digraphs. The test is whether the sequence is a LETTER OF THE ALPHABET, not merely one sound spelled with two characters.

da.note: None. AA is an old spelling of Å and appears in names, but is not a letter. The test is whether the sequence is a LETTER OF THE ALPHABET, not merely one sound spelled with two characters.

nb.note: None. The test is whether the sequence is a LETTER OF THE ALPHABET, not merely one sound spelled with two characters.

fi.note: None. The test is whether the sequence is a LETTER OF THE ALPHABET, not merely one sound spelled with two characters.

he.note: None. The five final forms — ך ם ן ף ץ — are shapes of existing letters, not separate ones. The test is whether the sequence is a LETTER OF THE ALPHABET, not merely one sound spelled with two characters.

not_applicable.note: Languages whose corpus was scanned and produced no candidates at all: da, el, fi, he, nb, ro, sv, tr, uk. Nothing to decide.

unscanned.note: Scanned in the iteration 1 analysis and found to contain candidates that are sounds rather than letters — es (LL, RR, CH), fr, it, pt, de. Recorded as reviewed above only where a decision was actually taken.
